mainTopic: Late מילה by day or night, רבי יוחנן's נוֹתָר rule, and who is fit for the rites of the פָּרָה אֲדוּמָּה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא in which רבי אלעזר בר שמעון says an on-time מילה must be by day, but a late מילה may be at night. The גמרא first suggests the dispute is about whether a מָשׁוּךְ needs מילה by Torah law. It rejects this and explains instead that the two sides argue over whether we learn from the extra ״וּבַיּוֹם״. רבי יוחנן teaches a similar rule about burning נוֹתָר. רבי אלעזר challenges him from a ברייתא and from the letters ו׳ and ה׳ in ״וְהַנּוֹתָר״, and רבי יוחנן is silent. A story follows: רבי יוחנן praises רבי אלעזר, ריש לקיש shows the teaching comes from תורת כהנים, and רבי יוחנן masters that work. רבי אלעזר then rules that an עָרֵל's sprinkling of פָּרָה אֲדוּמָּה water is valid, using a קל וחומר from a טְבוּל יוֹם. A ברייתא about a טוּמְטוּם seems to disagree, and רב יוסף assigns it to the school of רבי עקיבא, which treats an עָרֵל like a טָמֵא. The amud ends with the dispute between the רבנן and רבי יהודה about who may sanctify the water. They argue over how to read ״וְלָקְחוּ״ and ״וְנָתַן״, which explains why a קטן or a woman is fit or unfit.

steps.title: End of רבי אלעזר בר שמעון's ruling on late circumcision
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes רבי אלעזר בר שמעון's view: on time, a מילה is only by day; late, it may be by day or by night.
steps.simpleTranslation: [At its proper time] they may be circumcised only during the day. When it is not at its proper time, they may be circumcised during the day or at night.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing the quote of רבי אלעזר בר שמעון in the ברייתא. He splits between a מילה done on time and a מילה done late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בִּזְמַנּוֹ ("at its time") came just before this line. On time means the eighth day, and then the מילה must be by day. If the eighth day was missed, he allows the מילה even at night. The rest of this section tries to figure out why the תנא קמא disagrees with him.

keyTerms.meaning: At its proper time (for מילה, the eighth day)
Not at its proper time, meaning late
They are circumcised

phrases.english: they may be circumcised only during the day;
not at its proper time, they may be circumcised during the day or at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An on-time מילה is only by day. A late מילה may be by day or by night.

steps.title: Suggestion: the dispute is about whether a מָשׁוּךְ is Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the תנא קמא holds a מָשׁוּךְ needs מילה by Torah law, while רבי אלעזר בר שמעון holds it is only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they disagree about this: one Sage holds a מָשׁוּךְ needs circumcision by Torah law, and the other Sage holds a מָשׁוּךְ needs it only by rabbinic law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to show that the question of a מָשׁוּךְ is actually a dispute between the תנאים in this ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this suggestion, the תנא קמא requires daytime because he treats a מָשׁוּךְ's מילה as a real Torah מילה. רבי אלעזר בר שמעון allows night because to him it is only a rabbinic requirement. The difference between the two views would then be about the source of the obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that...? (opens a suggested reading)
They disagree
Someone whose foreskin was drawn forward to cover his מילה
By Torah law
By rabbinic law

phrases.english: Is it not that they disagree about this:
that one Sage holds a מָשׁוּךְ needs circumcision by Torah law,
phrases.notes: This 'one Sage' is the תנא קמא, who required daytime.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds a מָשׁוּךְ needs it only by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the ברייתא as a dispute about a מָשׁוּךְ.
steps.raayaObject: That whether a מָשׁוּךְ is Torah law is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר בר שמעון

steps.title: Rejection: a child past his eighth day surely needs מילה by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Nobody says a late child's מילה is only rabbinic, yet the תנאים argue about him too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really understand it that way? A child whose time has passed: is there anyone who says his circumcision is only rabbinic?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's dispute also covers a normal child whose eighth day was missed. Everyone agrees he must have a מילה by Torah law. So the 'Torah law versus rabbinic law' idea cannot explain why רבי אלעזר בר שמעון allows his מילה at night.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you understand it that way? (signals a rejection)
A child whose proper time for מילה has passed
Is there anyone who says...?

phrases.english: And can you really understand it that way?
A child whose proper time has passed:
is there anyone who says his circumcision is only rabbinic?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading offered in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that the dispute is about a מָשׁוּךְ
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's dispute also covers a late child, whose מילה is Torah law by everyone's view. So the suggested reason cannot explain the dispute.

steps.title: New explanation: they argue about learning from ״וּבַיּוֹם״
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees a מָשׁוּךְ is דרבנן and a late child is Torah law. They argue about whether the extra ״וּבַיּוֹם״ teaches that even a late מילה must be by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees: a מָשׁוּךְ is rabbinic, and a child whose time passed is Torah law. And here they disagree about this: one Sage holds we expound "and on the day," and the other Sage holds we do not expound "and on the day."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason for the dispute. It is about how to read a פסוק, not about Torah law versus rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ״וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי״ ("and on the eighth day"). The תנא קמא learns from the extra 'and' that every מילה, even a late one, must be by day. רבי אלעזר בר שמעון does not learn anything from it, so only the eighth-day מילה must be by day.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new explanation)
Everyone agrees
We expound, meaning we learn a law from the wording
"And on the day" (ויקרא 12:3)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a late child must have a מילה by Torah law. The only question is whether the extra 'and' in ״וּבַיּוֹם״ makes even a late מילה a daytime-only מילה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two explanations. The rejected one said the dispute was about a מָשׁוּךְ. The accepted one says everyone agrees about a מָשׁוּךְ, and the dispute is only about reading ״וּבַיּוֹם״.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees:
a מָשׁוּךְ needs circumcision only by rabbinic law,
and a child whose time has passed needs it by Torah law.
And here they disagree about this:
one Sage holds we expound "and on the day,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:3. The extra 'and' teaches that even a late מילה must be by day.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds we do not expound "and on the day."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation rejected in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the dispute to a different question: reading a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about whether a מָשׁוּךְ is Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees about a מָשׁוּךְ and about a late child. They argue only about whether the extra 'and' in ״וּבַיּוֹם״ teaches a law.

steps.title: A parallel: רבי יוחנן on burning נוֹתָר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that נוֹתָר burned at its proper time must be burned by day, but burned later may be burned by day or by night. This is the same kind of split as רבי אלעזר בר שמעון's.
steps.simpleTranslation: As in this teaching, where רבי יוחנן sat and expounded: נוֹתָר burned at its proper time may be burned only by day; burned not at its proper time, it may be burned by day or by night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another law that uses the same pattern: on time means daytime only, late means day or night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נוֹתָר is sacrificial meat left past its time, and it must be burned. רבי יוחנן says that burning it on its proper day must be by day, but after that it may be done at night too. This matches the reasoning of the view that does not expound ״וּבַיּוֹם״: the daytime rule applies only on the proper day.

keyTerms.meaning: He sat and expounded
Sacrificial meat left over past the time allowed for eating it
Is burned

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the split between 'at its time' and 'not at its time' is a pattern found in other areas of halacha, not something made up only for מילה.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּיָתֵיב רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְקָדָרֵישׁ:
phrases.english: As in this teaching, where רבי יוחנן sat and expounded:
נוֹתָר, burned at its proper time,
phrases.notes: נוֹתָר is offering meat left past its time, which must be burned. 'Its time' means the proper day for burning it.

phrases.english: may be burned only during the day;
not at its proper time,
it may be burned either during the day or at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּיָתֵיב רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְקָדָרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case with the same on-time versus late pattern as the view in step 4 that does not expound ״וּבַיּוֹם״.
steps.raayaObject: That a daytime rule can apply only at the proper time, and not afterward
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's teaching about burning נוֹתָר

steps.title: רבי אלעזר challenges רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא about late מילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר brings a ברייתא: ״וּבַיּוֹם״ teaches that even a מילה on day nine through twelve must be done by day. This is a problem for רבי יוחנן's rule that late-burned נוֹתָר may be burned at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר objected to רבי יוחנן: I would only know that a baby circumcised on the eighth day must be circumcised by day. How do I know to include the ninth, tenth, eleventh and twelfth days too? The verse says: "And on the day."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר attacks רבי יוחנן's rule from step 5 by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא says even a late מילה is only by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that something done late may be done at night. This ברייתא says the opposite about מילה: the extra ו׳ in ״וּבַיּוֹם״ stretches the daytime rule past day eight. If late מילה still needs daytime, why should late נוֹתָר be any different?

keyTerms.meaning: To include (an extra case)
The verse teaches
"And on the day", the extra word the ברייתא learns from

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar raised an objection to Rabbi Yoḥanan:
I would only know that one circumcised on the eighth day
is circumcised only by day;
from where do we include the ninth, the tenth,
the eleventh, the twelfth (from where)?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the extra word מִנַּיִן in round brackets and some leave it out. The meaning is the same either way.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And on the day."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:3. The extra ו׳ ("and") is what stretches the rule to later days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's נוֹתָר rule from step 5 using the ״וּבַיּוֹם״ reading from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that late-burned נוֹתָר may be burned by day or by night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says a late מילה still must be by day. By the same pattern, late burning of נוֹתָר should also be only by day.

steps.title: The letters ו׳ and ה׳ in ״וְהַנּוֹתָר״ teach the same rule, and רבי יוחנן is silent
steps.stepSummary: Someone might not learn anything from a single extra ו׳. But everyone learns from ו׳ together with ה׳, and ״וְהַנּוֹתָר״ has both. So נוֹתָר burned late also needs daytime. רבי יוחנן has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even someone who does not learn from an extra ו׳ does learn from ו׳ and ה׳ together. רבי יוחנן was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר closes a possible escape route, so the challenge applies directly to נוֹתָר. רבי יוחנן cannot answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might reply that not every תנא learns a law from one extra ו׳. רבי אלעזר answers that even such a תנא learns from ו׳ plus ה׳. The verse about נוֹתָר says ״וְהַנּוֹתָר״, with both letters, so it teaches that late burning is also by day. רבי יוחנן's silence means the objection stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Learns a law from (a word or letter in the verse)
The letters ו׳ and ה׳ together
He was silent (he had no answer)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר here is the אָמוֹרָא רבי אלעזר בן פדת, a student of רבי יוחנן. He is not the תַּנָּא רבי אלעזר בר שמעון from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: And even according to the one who does not expound a vav,
he does expound vav and heh.
phrases.notes: He means the word ״וְהַנּוֹתָר״ (ויקרא 7:17), which begins with both letters.

phrases.english: He was silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּלָא דָּרֵישׁ וָאו, וָאו וְהֵי דָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection of step 6 by applying it to the verse about נוֹתָר.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible defense of רבי יוחנן: that a single extra ו׳ teaches nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even the one who does not learn from ו׳ alone does learn from ו׳ and ה׳ together, and ״וְהַנּוֹתָר״ has both letters.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן praises רבי אלעזר to ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: After רבי אלעזר leaves, רבי יוחנן tells ריש לקיש that רבי אלעזר taught Torah as if he had heard it from משה straight from ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he left, רבי יוחנן said to ריש לקיש: I saw בן פדת sitting and expounding like משה from the mouth of the Almighty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the debate to a story. רבי יוחנן is deeply impressed by the challenge and praises his student. This sets up ריש לקיש's response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן thinks רבי אלעזר made up this reading of the verse himself. He calls it so precise that it is like Torah heard straight from ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of Pedat, meaning רבי אלעזר
From the mouth of the Almighty
רבי שמעון בן לקיש, רבי יוחנן's study partner

phrases.english: After he went out,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אלעזר.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to Reish Lakish:
I saw Ben Pedat sitting and expounding
like Moshe from the mouth of the Almighty.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּתַר דִּנְפַק, אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that reacts to the objection in steps 6 and 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן praises רבי אלעזר's teaching as being like Torah from Sinai.

steps.title: ריש לקיש shows it is a ברייתא, and רבי יוחנן masters תורת כהנים
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the teaching is not רבי אלעזר's own. It is a ברייתא from תורת כהנים. רבי יוחנן learns that whole work in three days and fully understands it in three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: Is it his own? It is a ברייתא. Where is it taught? In תורת כהנים. רבי יוחנן went out, learned it in three days, and understood it in three months.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש corrects רבי יוחנן's impression: רבי אלעזר was quoting an existing source. רבי יוחנן then goes and studies that source thoroughly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The praise was based on the idea that רבי אלעזר invented the reading of the verse. ריש לקיש points out it is an older ברייתא found in תורת כהנים, the מדרש on ויקרא. רבי יוחנן responds by learning the entire work, quickly at first and then in depth.

keyTerms.meaning: His own
A ברייתא (an outside teaching of the תנאים)
The מדרש on ויקרא, also called ספרא
He understood it in depth

steps.whatToRemember: The objection against רבי יוחנן's נוֹתָר rule comes from a ברייתא in תורת כהנים, and רבי יוחנן gave no answer to it.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to him:
Is it his own? It is a baraita.
Where is it taught? In Torat Kohanim.
He went out and learned it in three days,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יוחנן, and "it" is the whole of תורת כהנים.

phrases.english: and understood it in three months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the assumption behind רבי יוחנן's praise in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the idea that the reading was רבי אלעזר's own invention. The teaching itself stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The reading comes from an existing ברייתא in תורת כהנים.

steps.title: An עָרֵל who sprinkles פָּרָה אֲדוּמָּה water does so validly
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that if an עָרֵל sprinkled the purifying water, the sprinkling works. He compares this to a טְבוּל יוֹם, who may not eat תְּרוּמָה but is fit for the work of the פָּרָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: An עָרֵל who sprinkled, his sprinkling is valid. It is just like a טְבוּל יוֹם: even though he is forbidden to eat תְּרוּמָה, he is fit for the פָּרָה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic: a ruling by רבי אלעזר about the purifying water of the פָּרָה אֲדוּמָּה. An עָרֵל's sprinkling is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being an עָרֵל forbids a person from eating holy food like תְּרוּמָה. רבי אלעזר says that does not automatically disqualify him from the פָּרָה. A טְבוּל יוֹם is also barred from תְּרוּמָה, yet he is fit for the פָּרָה rites, so the עָרֵל is too.

keyTerms.meaning: An uncircumcised man
Sprinkled / the sprinkling of the purifying water
Someone who immersed today and is not fully pure until nightfall
The portion of produce given to a כֹּהֵן, eaten only in purity
The פָּרָה אֲדוּמָּה (red heifer) and its rites

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being forbidden from תְּרוּמָה does not by itself make a person unfit for every holy task.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
An uncircumcised man who sprinkled, his sprinkling is valid.
phrases.notes: This is the sprinkling of the פָּרָה אֲדוּמָּה water on someone impure from a dead body.

phrases.english: It is just like a tevul yom,
who, even though he is forbidden to eat teruma,
is fit for the heifer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the debate about doing things by day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עָרֵל's sprinkling of פָּרָה אֲדוּמָּה water is valid. Like a טְבוּל יוֹם, he is barred from תְּרוּמָה but fit for the פָּרָה.

steps.title: Maybe a טבול יום is better off than an ערל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's comparison. A טְבוּל יוֹם may eat מַעֲשֵׂר, but an עָרֵל may not, so you cannot learn the עָרֵל from the טְבוּל יוֹם.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a טְבוּל יוֹם? He is allowed to eat מַעֲשֵׂר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in רבי אלעזר's proof from a טְבוּל יוֹם. It says the טְבוּל יוֹם has an advantage the עָרֵל does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reasoned that if a טְבוּל יוֹם is fit for the פָּרָה, an עָרֵל should be fit too. But a טְבוּל יוֹם may eat מַעֲשֵׂר and an עָרֵל may not. So the טְבוּל יוֹם looks like the 'stronger' person, and being fit for the פָּרָה might come from that strength.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What about...?' A formula that points out a weakness in a comparison
Tithe. Here it means מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, which a טְבוּל יוֹם may eat
Someone who went to the מִקְוֶה today but is not fully pure until nightfall

phrases.english: What about one who immersed that day —
he is permitted to eat tithe!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison רבי אלעזר used in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's proof from טְבוּל יוֹם to עָרֵל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The טְבוּל יוֹם has an advantage (eating מַעֲשֵׂר) that the עָרֵל lacks, so the comparison breaks down.

steps.title: The comparison is about touching, not eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the comparison is about touching תְּרוּמָה. A טְבוּל יוֹם may not touch תְּרוּמָה and is still fit for the פָּרָה. An עָרֵל may touch תְּרוּמָה, so he should surely be fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Were we talking about eating? We were talking about touching. A טְבוּל יוֹם may not touch תְּרוּמָה, and he is still allowed to work with the פָּרָה. An עָרֵל may touch תְּרוּמָה, so surely he is allowed to work with the פָּרָה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר. It says the proof was never about eating. It was about touching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you compare touching, the עָרֵל is the stronger one. A טְבוּל יוֹם makes תְּרוּמָה פָּסוּל when he touches it, but an עָרֵל does not. So the קל וחומר works: if the weaker person (טְבוּל יוֹם) is fit for the פָּרָה, the stronger person (עָרֵל) is surely fit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that to say...?' A word that rejects the way the question understood the argument
Touching
'Is it not logical?' The ending of a קַל וָחוֹמֶר
The פָּרָה אֲדֻמָּה (red heifer) and the work of preparing and sprinkling its water

phrases.english: Were we speaking about eating?
We were speaking about touching:
If one who immersed that day, who is forbidden
to touch תרומה —
is still permitted to work with the heifer,
then an uncircumcised man, who is allowed to touch —
is it not logical that he is permitted to work with the heifer?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by explaining which point is being compared.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the basis of the comparison (touching instead of eating)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The questioner thought the comparison was about eating, where a טְבוּל יוֹם is better off.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison is about touching, where an עָרֵל is better off, so the קל וחומר stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The קל וחומר: a טְבוּל יוֹם may not touch תְּרוּמָה but is fit for the פָּרָה. An עָרֵל may touch תְּרוּמָה, so he is surely fit for the פָּרָה.

steps.title: A ברייתא and a real case support רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also says an עָרֵל's sprinkling is valid, and there was a real case where the חכמים approved it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same thing: if an עָרֵל sprinkled, his sprinkling is valid. And this really happened, and the חכמים approved his sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now רבי אלעזר's ruling rested on logic. Now a ברייתא says the same thing, and it even reports a real case where the חכמים approved such a sprinkling.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is also taught so.' A ברייתא that supports what was just said
Sprinkling the purifying water on a טָמֵא person
'There was an incident.' A real case that happened

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
An uncircumcised man who sprinkled — his sprinkling is valid.
And there was an incident,
and the Sages declared his sprinkling valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that supports the ruling just defended.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's ruling that an עָרֵל's sprinkling is valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא and a real case where the חכמים approved such a sprinkling

steps.title: A ברייתא says an ערל may not prepare the water
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a טוּמְטוּם who prepared the water did an invalid job, because he might be an עָרֵל, and an עָרֵל may not prepare it. This seems to go against רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא challenges this. A ברייתא teaches: if a טוּמְטוּם prepared the water, it is invalid, because he might be an עָרֵל, and an עָרֵל may not prepare it. If an אַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס prepared it, it is valid. רבי יהודה says: even if an אַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס prepared it, it is invalid, because he might be a woman, and a woman may not prepare it. In any case, the ברייתא teaches that an עָרֵל, and even a person who might be an עָרֵל, may not prepare the water!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to argue with רבי אלעזר. It says an עָרֵל is not fit to prepare the פָּרָה water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא disqualifies a טוּמְטוּם only because he might be an עָרֵל. So it must hold that a definite עָרֵל is not fit for the work of the פָּרָה. That clashes with רבי אלעזר, who said an עָרֵל is fit.

keyTerms.meaning: A person whose body is covered so we cannot tell if he is male or female
A person with both male and female features
Here: preparing the water by putting the ashes of the פָּרָה into it
'In any case it teaches.' Points to the one detail in the source that matters for the challenge

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two jobs. קִידּוּשׁ here means putting the ashes into the water, and הַזָּאָה means sprinkling the water. Neither word here means marriage.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A טומטום who prepared the water — his preparing is invalid,
phrases.notes: 'Prepared' here means putting the ashes into the water.

phrases.english: because he might be uncircumcised,
and an uncircumcised man is unfit to prepare the water.
But an אנדרוגינוס who prepared it — his preparing is valid.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even an אנדרוגינוס who prepared it — his preparing is invalid,
because he might be a woman,
phrases.notes: Some versions add the word in square brackets, 'he is'. It does not change the meaning.

phrases.english: and a woman is unfit to prepare the water.
In any case, it teaches:
an uncircumcised man, and one who might be uncircumcised, is unfit to prepare the water!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that seems to disagree with the ruling that steps 12-13 supported.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that an עָרֵל is fit for the work of the פָּרָה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא disqualifies a טוּמְטוּם only because he might be an עָרֵל. That shows a definite עָרֵל is unfit for the work of the פָּרָה.

steps.title: That ברייתא follows the school of רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the טוּמְטוּם ברייתא follows the school of רבי עקיבא, who learns from ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ that an עָרֵל is treated like a טָמֵא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This תַּנָּא is from the school of רבי עקיבא, who treats an עָרֵל like a טָמֵא person. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי עקיבא says, ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ comes to include an עָרֵל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge. He says the ברייתא that disqualifies an עָרֵל follows one specific opinion, that of רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא reads the doubled word ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ (ויקרא 22:4) as including an עָרֵל together with a טָמֵא. So in his view an עָרֵל is like a טָמֵא and cannot do the work of the פָּרָה. רבי אלעזר and the supporting ברייתא simply do not follow רבי עקיבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A תַּנָּא from the study house of רבי עקיבא
Includes. Learns from the פסוק that an extra case belongs in the law
'Any man.' The doubled word in the פסוק that רבי עקיבא uses to include an עָרֵל

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views. רבי אלעזר and the supporting ברייתא say an עָרֵל is fit for the פָּרָה. The school of רבי עקיבא treats an עָרֵל like a טָמֵא and says he is unfit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer shows that the clash between the two sources is a real argument between תַּנָּאִים. It is not a mistake in רבי אלעזר's ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא — תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הוּא,
phrases.english: This tanna is a tanna from the school of Rabbi Akiva,
who includes the uncircumcised man as being like one who is impure.
As it is taught: Rabbi Akiva says:
"Any man" comes to include the uncircumcised man.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:4

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף הַאי תַּנָּא תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by saying which תַּנָּא that ברייתא follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the challenging source to a specific תַּנָּא (רבי עקיבא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to state the accepted halacha against רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who treats an עָרֵל like a טָמֵא. רבי אלעזר follows the other view.

steps.title: רבא asks why no source lists the עָרֵל with the טָמֵא
steps.stepSummary: רבא recalls that while sitting before רב יוסף he was bothered. If רבי עקיבא really treats an עָרֵל like a טָמֵא, some תנא should have taught them together, and we could say it follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I was sitting before רב יוסף and I had a difficulty. Shouldn't some תנא somewhere have taught 'the עָרֵל and the טָמֵא' together, so that we could say it follows רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a difficulty with רב יוסף's answer from Step 15. If רבי עקיבא treats an עָרֵל like a טָמֵא, we would expect to find a ברייתא that lists them together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said the טוּמְטוּם ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who treats an עָרֵל like a טָמֵא. רבא argues that if such a view existed, we would expect at least one source pairing 'הערל והטמא'. Since none seems to exist, רב יוסף's answer looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: I had a difficulty
let it slip out, show up somewhere
a teacher of the משנה or ברייתא period
the uncircumcised and the ritually impure

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: הֲוָה יָתֵיבְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: Rava said: I was sitting before Rav Yosef,
and I had a difficulty:
should no tanna let it slip out
phrases.notes: Literally 'slip out.' He means: shouldn't at least one תנא somewhere have said it?

phrases.english: and teach 'the uncircumcised and the impure' together,
so that we would say it is Rabbi Akiva?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַשְׁיָא לִי: לָא לִישְׁתְּמִיט תַּנָּא וְלִיתְנֵי הֶעָרֵל וְהַטָּמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer in Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that רבי עקיבא treats an עָרֵל like a טָמֵא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If this view existed, some ברייתא should list the עָרֵל and the טָמֵא together, and none seems to.

steps.title: There is a source listing them together: exemption from coming to the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רבא: there is such a ברייתא. It says the עָרֵל and the טָמֵא are exempt from appearing in the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no such source? But a ברייתא teaches: the עָרֵל and the טָמֵא are exempt from ראייה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבא's claim that no source pairs the עָרֵל with the טָמֵא. It quotes a ברייתא that does exactly that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed there was no such pairing. This ברייתא lists both together as exempt from ראייה, which seems to be the very source רבא was looking for. That would support רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: And is there not? (questioning the claim)
the מצוה to appear in the בית המקדש on the three רגלים
exempt

phrases.english: And is there not?
But it is taught:
The uncircumcised and the impure are exempt from appearing!
phrases.notes: This means appearing in the בית המקדש on פסח, שבועות and סוכות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's claim from Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that no תנא pairs the עָרֵל with the טָמֵא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא about ראייה lists them side by side.

steps.title: That source has a different reason: the עָרֵל is repulsive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The עָרֵל is exempt from ראייה only because he is repulsive, not because he is like a טָמֵא.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the reason is that he is repulsive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from the ראייה ברייתא. The עָרֵל and the טָמֵא share the same ruling there, but each for his own reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עָרֵל is exempt from coming to the עזרה because it is not fitting for someone repulsive to appear there. That has nothing to do with טומאה. So this ברייתא does not show anyone treating an עָרֵל like a טָמֵא, and רבא's difficulty stands.

keyTerms.meaning: there (in that case)
repulsive, disgusting

steps.confusionAlert: Two people can share the same ruling for totally different reasons. Being listed together does not mean an עָרֵל has the status of a טָמֵא.

phrases.english: There it is because he is repulsive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge brought in Step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the ראייה ברייתא as a source that an עָרֵל is like a טָמֵא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The exemption comes from the עָרֵל being repulsive, not from any טומאה status.

steps.title: The רבנן and רבי יהודה follow their usual views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the רבנן and רבי יהודה are consistent. It quotes a ברייתא: everyone may sanctify the water except a חרש, שוטה and קטן. רבי יהודה allows a קטן but forbids a woman and an אנדרוגינוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: They follow their own reasoning. As a ברייתא teaches: all are fit to sanctify the water except a חרש, a שוטה and a קטן. רבי יהודה deems a קטן fit, but deems a woman and an אנדרוגינוס unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the part of the earlier ברייתא about an אנדרוגינוס preparing the water. It shows that the רבנן and רבי יהודה rule the same way in another ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא (with the טוּמְטוּם) also ruled on an אנדרוגינוס. The רבנן allowed him and רבי יהודה did not. Here we see the source of that split: the רבנן allow even a woman to sanctify, while רבי יהודה invalidates a woman, so an אנדרוגינוס, who might be a woman, is also invalid for him.

keyTerms.meaning: they follow their own reasoning (they are consistent)
to sanctify: placing the פרה אדומה ashes into the water
deaf-mute, mentally incompetent person, and minor
a person with both male and female features

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning.
phrases.notes: 'They' are the רבנן and רבי יהודה, who argued in the earlier ברייתא about an אנדרוגינוס preparing the water.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
All are fit to sanctify
phrases.notes: To sanctify means putting the פרה אדומה ashes into the water.

phrases.english: except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor.
Rabbi Yehuda deems a minor fit
but deems a woman and a hermaphrodite unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the עָרֵל question to the אנדרוגינוס part of the earlier ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, everyone except a חרש, שוטה and קטן may sanctify, including a woman. רבי יהודה allows a קטן but invalidates a woman and an אנדרוגינוס.

steps.title: What is the רבנן's reason for their list of who may sanctify
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the רבנן's view that a woman may sanctify the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks for the source of the רבנן's rule about who may sanctify the water (a קטן is unfit, a woman is fit). The next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן's rule in step 19 has two sides: a קטן is unfit, yet a woman is fit. The גמרא wants the source for that rule. רבי יהודה's view is explained later, in steps 22-24.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?
the majority of the Sages

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the רבנן's view in Step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the רבנן's rule that a קטן is unfit to sanctify the water while a woman is fit

steps.title: Sanctifying follows the same rules as gathering the ashes
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק links taking the ashes to placing the water. So whoever is unfit to gather the ashes is unfit to sanctify, and whoever is fit to gather is fit to sanctify.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And they shall take for the impure from the ashes of the burning of the sin-offering.' Those unfit for gathering are unfit for sanctifying, and those fit for gathering are fit for sanctifying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 20 with a פסוק. The פסוק ties sanctifying the water to gathering the ashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק puts taking the ashes and placing the water together, the same people qualify for both jobs. Since a woman is fit to gather the ashes, the רבנן hold she is also fit to sanctify the water.

keyTerms.meaning: gathering the ashes of the פרה אדומה
sanctifying: putting the ashes into the water
the ashes of the burned פרה אדומה
those

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, sanctifying the water follows the rules of gathering the ashes. Whoever may gather may sanctify, so a woman may do both.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the רבנן allow an אנדרוגינוס to prepare the water: even if he is a woman, a woman is fit.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And they shall take for the impure
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:17. The same פסוק goes on to talk about putting running water in a vessel.

phrases.english: from the ashes of the burning of the sin-offering",
those who are unfit for gathering
are unfit for sanctification;
those who are fit for gathering
are fit for sanctification.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְלָקְחוּ לַטָּמֵא מֵעֲפַר שְׂרֵיפַת הַחַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links gathering the ashes with sanctifying the water, so the same people are fit or unfit for both.

steps.title: רבי יהודה reads the plural word as separating the two jobs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if the two jobs were meant to be linked, the פסוק would have said ״וְלָקַח״ in the singular. The plural ״וְלָקְחוּ״ teaches that people unfit to gather the ashes are still fit to sanctify the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה would answer you: If so, the פסוק should have said 'and he shall take.' Why does it say 'and they shall take'? To teach that even those who are unfit there are fit here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יהודה would answer the רבנן's proof from the פסוק. He uses the same פסוק to reach the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said the פסוק links taking the ashes to placing the water. רבי יהודה points out a mismatch: ״וְלָקְחוּ״ is plural but ״וְנָתַן״ is singular. That change shows the two jobs follow different rules, so a קטן who cannot gather may still sanctify.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they shall take' (plural), the word in the פסוק about taking the ashes
'And he shall take' (singular), the word רבי יהודה says would have been used if the jobs were linked
Unfit, not allowed to do the job
Fit, allowed to do the job
There / here: gathering the ashes / sanctifying the water

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides use the SAME פסוק. The רבנן see a link between the two jobs. רבי יהודה sees the plural-singular change as a sign that the jobs are different.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda would say to you:
If so, let the verse say "and he shall take" (singular),
phrases.notes: 'If so' means if taking and placing really were linked. Then both words should match, like ״וְנָתַן״ (במדבר 19:17).

phrases.english: What is the point of "and they shall take" (plural)?
It teaches that even those who are unfit there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means gathering the ashes, where a קטן is unfit.

phrases.english: are fit here, for sanctifying the water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's derivation in step 21 by reading the same פסוק the other way, explaining רבי יהודה's view from step 19 that a קטן may sanctify.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the פסוק (singular vs. plural)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק links gathering and sanctifying, so a קטן, who is unfit to gather, cannot sanctify.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural ״וְלָקְחוּ״ separates the jobs, so those unfit to gather are fit to sanctify.

steps.title: Then a woman should also be fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: if people unfit to gather may sanctify, a woman should also be fit to sanctify.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a woman should also be fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יהודה's reading. It points out that his reading seems to allow a woman too, even though he forbids her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19, רבי יהודה forbade a woman to sanctify. But his new rule says that being unfit for gathering does not matter for sanctifying. So why should a woman be any different from a קטן?

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is true
A woman
Also, too

phrases.english: If so, a woman should also be fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the logic of רבי יהודה's reading from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's reading that those unfit to gather are fit to sanctify
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If his rule is true, a woman should also be fit to sanctify, but he forbids her (step 19).

steps.title: The verse says he places, not she places
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה excludes a woman because the פסוק uses the masculine word ״וְנָתַן״ and not the feminine ״וְנָתְנָה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says 'and he shall place,' and not 'and she shall place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יהודה. The word for placing the water is masculine, so a woman is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural ״וְלָקְחוּ״ opens the door for people unfit to gather, like a קטן. But the masculine ״וְנָתַן״ is about the sanctifying job itself, and it limits that job to males. So a קטן is fit and a woman is not.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall place' (masculine), the word in the פסוק about putting the water on the ashes
'And she shall place' (feminine), a word the פסוק does NOT use

phrases.english: "And he shall place," and not "and she shall place."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the gender of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's rule should let a woman sanctify too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The masculine ״וְנָתַן״ excludes a woman from sanctifying.

steps.title: The רבנן: the plural shows one person need not do both jobs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן deal with ״וְנָתַן״. They answer that if the פסוק had said ״וְלָקַח״ and ״וְנָתַן״, we would think the same one person must take and place. So the Torah wrote ״וְלָקְחוּ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? If it were written 'and he shall take' and 'and he shall place,' I would have said one person takes and that same person places. So the Merciful One wrote 'and they shall take.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks how the רבנן explain the mix of plural and singular words. It begins their answer: the plural ״וְלָקְחוּ״ teaches that taking and placing do not have to be done by the same person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used the plural-singular change to learn his own rules. The רבנן say the change teaches something else entirely. With two singular words, we would think one person must do the whole process. The plural shows that more than one person may be involved.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought, the mistaken idea the Torah's wording prevents
Takes (singular)
Gives / places (singular)
'The Merciful One,' meaning the Torah / ה׳

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: This is a short question: how would the רבנן explain these singular and plural words?

phrases.english: If it were written "and he shall take" and "and he shall place,"

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא שָׁקֵיל חַד וְיָהֵיב חַד,
phrases.english: I would have said that one takes and that same one places,
so the Merciful One wrote "and they shall take."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Switches back to the רבנן and explains the plural word in a way that does not support רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each wording is needed for its own lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With ״וְלָקַח״ and ״וְנָתַן״, the same single person would have to take and place.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״וְלָקְחוּ״ teaches that more than one person may take the ashes.

steps.title: The רבנן: two may take and one may place
steps.stepSummary: If both words were plural, we would think two people must take and two must place. So the Torah wrote ״וְלָקְחוּ״ and ״וְנָתַן״: even if two take, one person may place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Merciful One had written 'and they shall take' and 'and they shall place,' I would have said that two take and two place. So the Merciful One wrote 'and they shall take' and 'and he shall place': even if two take, one may place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the רבנן's answer. The exact mix, plural for taking and singular for placing, is needed to teach that two may take and one may place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two plural words would suggest that two people are required for each job. The plural-then-singular wording teaches that two may take the ashes while one places the water. Since ״וְנָתַן״ is needed for this lesson, the רבנן do not use it to exclude a woman, and their link between the two jobs stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they shall place' (plural), a word the פסוק does NOT use
Two
One

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה reads ״וְלָקְחוּ״ as separating the jobs, so a קטן may sanctify, and ״וְנָתַן״ as excluding a woman. The רבנן say the plural-singular wording only teaches that two may take and one may place. So for them a woman is fit and a קטן is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic גמרא pattern: one side reads an odd wording as a special teaching, and the other side shows the wording is needed for a different, practical lesson.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written "and they shall take" and "and they shall place,"

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא דְּשָׁקְלִי תְּרֵי וְיָהֲבִי תְּרֵי,
phrases.english: I would have said that two must take and two must place,
so the Merciful One wrote "and they shall take" and "and he shall place":
that even if two take, one may place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רבנן's explanation begun in step 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For the רבנן, the plural-singular wording teaches that two may take and one may place, so ״וְנָתַן״ does not exclude a woman.
